title: Mosaic cache experiments — personal notes (Devin Huang)
content:
Goal
----
Sketch and running TODOs for a lightweight, composable KV-cache compression approach I’m calling ‘mosaic cache’ — combine episodic compressed segments + short-window specialists so long-context apps keep most signal while reducing memory/IO and quantized runtime cost. This is my personal exploration notes before a short proto sprint.

Motivation / intuition
--------------------
- Long-context inference on production workloads is dominated by KV-cache memory bandwidth and attention compute for full-context tokens.
- A single, monolithic compressed cache has tradeoffs: either you compress too aggressively (lossy -> hallucinations/regression) or you keep too much (no cost wins).
- Idea: split the context into semantically coherent segments (recent dialogue turns, retrieved passages, persistent user profile, tool outputs). Compress each segment with a different profile and keep a small, fast shortlist of uncompressed recent tokens for low-latency attention.
- I call this composition pattern ‘mosaic’ because pieces use different compression knobs and are stitched at runtime.

Key research questions
----------------------
1) Quality vs compression curve by segment type: how tolerant are retrieved docs vs. short-term convo for quantization / pruning?
2) Behavior under chain-of-thought (CoT) and multi-step plans — does segment compression break internal reasoning?
3) Cache eviction / refresh policy: dynamic scoring vs static TTL vs usage-based keep.
4) Runtime complexity: can we implement mixture-of-kernels so token attention falls back to specialized fast paths per-segment?

Quick literature hits to read (prioritize)
--------------------------------------
- Sparse attention + local-global hybrids (recent NeurIPS/ICLR surveys) — to get background on mixing full and local attention.
- Papers on quantization-robust prompting and probe regressions (arXiv 25xx) — helps build evaluation criteria.
- Episodic memory papers (RAG variants with compressed indices) — compare retrieval compression to KV compression.
- Practical blog: "Trading off KV cache fidelity for latency" (internal notes linked above).

Hypotheses (a few testable ones)
--------------------------------
- H1: Retrieved documents tolerate ~2–4 bits quantization with small downstream ROUGE/EM loss when paired with reranker re-querying.
- H2: CoT steps that rely on immediate token recurrence (recent 128 tokens) suffer disproportionately from compression — so short-window uncompressed cache is required.
- H3: A hybrid mosaic (uncompressed 256 tokens + per-doc 4-bit compressed segments + 8-bit persistent profile) yields ~30–45% memory saving with <3% useful-answer degradation on retrieval-heavy tasks.

Experiment plan (minimal viable)
--------------------------------
1) Bench dataset: create 3 slices — conversational multi-turn (Redwood chat logs w/ opt-in), RAG QA pairs (open-domain), and instruction-with-calcs (CoT prone). Use 2k examples each.
2) Baselines: full-precision KV cache; 8-bit quantized monolithic cache; no-cache (small context window).
3) Mosaic variants: (A) short-uncompressed 128 + per-doc 4-bit; (B) short-uncompressed 256 + per-doc 6-bit + persistent 8-bit; (C) dynamic eviction based on token access frequency.
4) Models: run on a 7B and 13B open model (same model family), use the same tokenizer and kernel. Keep decoding beam/temperature fixed.
5) Metrics: accuracy/EM/ROUGE, perplexity on held-back context reconstructions, CoT step fidelity (custom token-aligned tests), token-throughput (tokens/sec), memory and GPU VRAM, tail latency (p95/p99). Also subjective hallucination tags via small human eval sample (50 examples per slice).

Implementation notes / engineering constraints
-------------------------------------------
- KV layout: keep per-layer short index of segment descriptors (segment start, length, compression codec id). This must be small.
- Codec candidates: 4-bit quant (LSQ-like), vectorwise product quantization (PQ) on KV rows, top-k sparsification of low-salience heads.
- Runtime: need to ensure we can perform mixed-attention where queries hit uncompressed short window first, then selectively fetch / dequantize only the top-k segments based on attention score (approx inner product). This implies fast lightweight scoring step (FP16 dot prod on compressed proxies).
- Hardware: experiments on a single A100/80GB (local dev) + small multi-GPU sim to measure cross-GPU IO. Estimate memory for baseline 13B full-cache: ~45GB for full past 2048 tokens; target mosaic compressed: <25GB.

Quick TODOs (first run)
----------------------
- [ ] Script data slice creation and annotation for CoT fidelity tests (Devin) — due 2026-03-28.
- [ ] Implement lightweight segment descriptor in runtime shim (Tessa) — prototype 1: a JSON-backed descriptor list, no persistence.
- [ ] Add 4-bit quant codec adapter to existing KV serializer (Kai) — reuse q8 tool from quant-experiments repo.
- [ ] Create small eval harness to compute token-reconstruction perplexity and model output diffs (Devin + Kai).
- [ ] Schedule a 1-hour sync after first run to pick best variant and iterate.

Risks / unknowns
----------------
- Dequantization cost might cancel memory savings at inference throughput; need to measure end-to-end tokens/sec not just compressed size.
- Complexity of segmented attention could increase tail latency if naive. Must prototype scoring + lazy dequant.
- Edge-case regression where compression subtly changes decoding trajectory causing plausible-but-wrong answers — this is the most dangerous issue for customer-facing apps.

Mini thought-experiments / heuristics
-----------------------------------
- If a retrieved doc is only used for one or two attention hops, tiny errors can be tolerated; if retrieval seed anchors a chain-of-thought (multiple hops), keep it higher fidelity. So usage frequency and hop-depth should be tracked and dictate codec.
- For dialogue: user identity/profile sections can be aggressively compressed if we also keep the last N turns uncompressed.

Notes to self (fragments)
------------------------
- Try PQ on key vectors only vs both K+V — maybe keys are more sensitive to dot-product scoring, values more tolerant.
- Think about indexing compressed segments on an LRU + importance score for eviction. Maybe use a cheap learned scorer (tiny MLP) trained on past access traces.
- Could pair mosaic with upstream reranker that promotes segments to high-fidelity on re-query. That avoids always keeping everything high fidelity.

Conversation points for sync
---------------------------
- What codec primitives already in infra? Can we reuse q8 pipeline?
- Would SRE be OK running this on Dedicated clusters as a feature flag? Concern: memory profiling and p95 spikes.
- Are there ML-priors we can inject to choose codec per-segment (head salience, semantic density)?

References / readings I want to finish before prototype
----------------------------------------------------
- "Adaptive Compression for Transformer Memory" (arXiv) — focus on their eval suite.
- "Compressed RAG indices" blog — good practical heuristics.
- Internal: quant-experiments repo PR #14 (Kai) — check edge-case regressions noted.

Bottom line / next steps
-----------------------
Mosaic feels promising for middle-ground customers who need >8k context but can’t afford full-fidelity for all tokens. First sprint objective: demonstrate a 30% reduction in VRAM for 13B with <5% end-task regressions on RAG+chat slices. If good, we can push an RFC for a prototype runtime path and a small internal beta.

End of notes.

Minor changes log:
- 2026-03-24: added CoT fidelity test plan
- 2026-03-29: refined metric list and added PQ idea for K vs V
- 2026-04-02: bumped target memory saving target and scheduled proto sync
